newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria launches oil and gas export free zone.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria launches oil and gas export free zone.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has launched an oil and gas export free zone in the southeastern oil-producing port of Onne-Ikpokiri, officials said on Monday.

They said transport minister Major-General Ibrahim Gumel declared the zone open at the weekend and called on all oil firms to invest in the area which was also designed to service West and Central Africa.

With the launch of the zone, the cost of oil business in Nigeria would be substantially reduced while the commercial and investment portfolio of the oil industry's upstream sector would increase, Gumel was quoted by the semi-official Daily Times newspaper as saying.
The government signed a decree in November to establish the zone which it said was aimed at creating a climate conducive to investment in the oil and gas sector, Nigeria's economic backbone.
Gumel said granting a free port status to Onne would enable oil and gas companies to import equipment for their operations without going through the normal clearing procedures.

"My ministry will soon embark on a rail project to link the Federal Ocean Terminal at Onne with Port-Harcourt," he said adding that plans were on to turn the Onne and Port-Harcourt highway into dual carriage way.
Construction of an export processing zone (EPZ) has almost been completed in Calabar, also in the southeast.
Officials said the site was reasonably ready for six firms already given licences to operate there.

The EPZ, which will provide a self-regulatory economic zone where goods would be produced primarily for the export market, is aimed at encouraging foreign investment and diversifying Nigeria's oil-dependent economy.
Nigeria produces nearly two million barrels of crude oil per day from which it derives slightly more than 90 percent of its foreign exchange earnings.
